previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for shortness of breath and hypoxia. Imaging revealed bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with pneumonia, likely hospital-acquired or aspiration-related, though she was not found to be at aspiration risk. She was treated with a 7-day course of levofloxacin and supplemental oxygen, with improvement in oxygenation to 92% on room air by discharge. Her chronic pain, exacerbated by recent discontinuation of Lyrica and gabapentin, was addressed by restarting pregabalin at 75mg twice daily. A topical antifungal was used for urinary discomfort, which resolved. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable throughout. Medications were reconciled to reflect her actual home regimen. She was discharged home with services and follow-up planned.

The patient is a ___ year old female with history of T1-T2 
paraplegia requiring intermittent straight cath with history of

urine culture recently growing Klebsiella, not treated prior 
given pt had been asymptomatic up until day of admission. CXR on 
admission showed resolving bibasilar atelectasis, no new 
infiltrate. Pt had SBP in ___ over the night of admission, 
afebrile. Hypotension felt to be likely either due to 
infectious/vasodilatory effect vs. dehydration in setting of 
poor po intake and loose stools. Received 3 L NS bolus over 
night of admission, Zosyn in ED to cover for UTI, and Meropenem 
on the floor. SBP the following day was back up into the 100s. 
UTI treated as per below. 
.
#. UTI, bacterial: Patient with known urine cultures growing 
ESBL Klebsiella this past week from the ___. Overnight 
hospitalist contacted Micro lab and confirmed ESBL Klebsiella, 
sensitive to Imipenem at the ___. Pt presented with 
leukocytosis and sysytemic symptoms as manifested by altered 
mental status, prudent to treat. Started on meropenem on ___. 
Urine culture here grew Klebsiella, multi-drug resistant. 
Requested carbopenem sensitivities on this (not yet done prior 
to discharge). Given pt was clinically improved by discharge, 
presume antibiotics have been effective. Meropenem was changed 
to ertapenem prior to discharge for ease of dosing. PICC line 
was placed and will treat for 10 day course given complicated 
UTI. Pt can resumed straight intermittent catheterization at 
discharge.
.
# Delirium: Per pts caregiver, she was very confused prior to 
admission, resolved on morning after admission here. Likely due 
to infection. Of note, patient and PCA reported headache the 
morning prior to admission and neck pain that has been ongoing x 
1 week. The patient was mildly lethargic but generally 
appropriate on exam. Cranial nerve examination was normal and 
there was no evidence of meningismus on exam. Given more likely 
infectious source by way of urine, meningitis felt to be of low 
likelihood. Pts delirium resolved by the morning after 
admission.

.
# Diarrhea: Pt had loose stools the day prior to admission, and 
some while here. She continued to ask for stool softeners while 
here, likely contributing. C diff was negative x1. Per pt, she 
sometimes also has loose stools while on antibiotics.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with new onset chills, recent pneumonia,
evaluate for pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  ___.

UPRIGHT FRONTAL VIEW, CHEST:  There are multiple old healed rib fractures and
related distortion of the bony thorax.  Bilateral humeral hardware is
partially visualized.

The lungs are better aerated than prior study with mild residual ill-defined
opacity at both lung bases which could represent resolving atelectasis.  There
are no new consolidations, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax.  Heart size is
borderline but unchanged.  There is no pulmonary edema.

IMPRESSION:  Interval improvement in the parenchymal aeration with mild
residual ill-defined opacities at both bases which could reflect resolving
atelectasis and/or infection.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ with UTI requiring antibiotics.  Request is
made for PICC line placement.

FOLLOWUP:  Dr. ___.

STAFF RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ reviewed the study.

SEDATION:  1% lidocaine was used for local anesthesia.

PROCEDURE:  The right upper arm was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.  Access was obtained into the right basilic vein under ultrasound
guidance with a micropuncture needle.  The 0.018 wire would not pass.  A
venogram was performed, which demonstrated spasming of the vessel.  The access
was reobtained into the basilic vein.  A hard copy ultrasound images were
obtained before and after access.  This time, an 0.018 Glidewire was placed
through the needle and advanced into the SVC.  The needle was removed and
replaced with a 5 ___ peel-away sheath.  The wire was then replaced with
the nitinol wire.  A new 37 cm 5 ___ double-lumen PICC line was advanced
over the wire until its tip was in the SVC.  The sheath was peeled away and
the wire was removed.  The final position of the tip at the SVC.  The final
length is 37 cm.  A sterile dressing was applied.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Placement of 5 ___ double-lumen PICC line via right basilic
vein with tip in the SVC.
